Daily Quiz.question: ১) "The Odd Women" is a novel written by -
Daily Quiz.exp:
George Robert Gissing:
English novelist, noted for the unflinching realism of his novels about the lower middle class. 

The Odd Women:
The novel was published in 1893.Its themes are the role of women in society, marriage, morals and the early feminist movement.

Notable Works of Geroge Robert Gissing:
- Born in Exile,
- The Nether World,
- Denzil Quarrier,
- The Odd Women,
- The Paying Guest,
- The Whirlpool,
- Charles Dickens: A Critical Study.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) Who is considered to be the chief representative poet of the Victorian Age?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Alfred, Lord Tennyson, in full Alfred Tennyson, 1st Baron Tennyson of Aldworth and Freshwater is often regarded as the chief representative poet of the Victorian period. 
- Born in 1809 and died in 1892
- His poetry is remarkable for its metrical variety, rich imagery, and verbal melodies.
- He is best known for his melodious language use in Poetry
- He received a Doctor of Law from Oxford University.

Best Works: 
- Poems (1833)
- In memoriam {Elegy, (1850) }: ১৩১ টা সেকশনব্যাপী বিশাল দীর্ঘ কবিতা এটি। এই কবিতাটি তিনি রচনা করেন মূলত: তার বন্ধু Hallam এর মৃত্যুশোকে। 
- Crossing the Bar
- Demeter and Other Poems
- Enoch Arden
- Idylls of the King
- Locksley Hall
- Mariana
- Maud and Other Poems
- Chiefly Lyrical
- Poems by Two Brothers
- The Charge of the Light Brigade
- The Lady of Shalott
- The Lotos-Eaters
- The Princess
- The Promise of May
- Ulysses 

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) My Last Duchess is -
Daily Quiz.exp:
My Last Duchess:
My Last Duchess, poem of 56 lines in rhyming couplets by Robert Browning, published in 1842 in Dramatic Lyrics, a volume in his Bells and Pomegranates series.
It is one of Browning’s most successful dramatic monologues.

Robert Browning: (1812-89)
- One of the major English poets of the Victorian age, noted for his mastery of dramatic -monologue and psychological portraiture. 
- He is famous for his dramatic monologues. So, he is often called the father of dramatic monologue.
- His wife Elizabeth Barrett was also a poet of that time. 

Notable Works:

Books of poems:
- Men and Women 
- Dramatic Lyrics
- The Ring of the Book. 

Other Poems: 
- Bishop Blougram’s Apology
- Christmas-Eve and Easter-Day
- Dramatis Personae
- Fra Lippo Lippi
- Men and Women
- My Last Duchess

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.exp:
A Tale of Two cities:

A Tale of Two Cities is a novel by Charles Dickens. The story is set in the late 18th century against the background of the French Revolution.
The novel depicts the sprawling tale of London and revolutionary Paris.

Chief Characters:

- Lucie Manette,
- Charles Darnay,
- Sydney Carton,

- Jerry Cruncher,
- Ernest Defarge,
- Mr. Lorry
- Ernest Defarge: The owner of a wine-shop in a Paris suburb. Defarge is a leader of the Jacquerie (a roving band of peasants) during the French Revolution.

Charles Dickens: 
- He was born in 1812 and died in 1870.
- Charles Dickens is considered the greatest English novelist of the Victorian era.
- His Father was a Clerk. 
- Charles Dickens worked as a journalist, writing numerous items on political and social affairs.

Best Works:

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) "Sentimental Education" by Gustave Flaubert is _____.
Daily Quiz.exp:
Sentimental Education:
- Sentimental Education (French: L'Éducation sentimentale, 1869) is a novel by Gustave Flaubert. Considered one of the most influential novels of the 19th century. 
- The novel describes the life of a young man (Frédéric Moreau) living through the revolution of -1848 and the founding of the Second French Empire, and his love for an older woman.

Gustave Flaubert: (1821-1880):
One of the great French novelists, regarded as the prime mover of the realist school of French literature and best known for his masterpiece novels. 

Best Works: 
- A Sentimental Education
- Bouvard and Pécuchet” 
- Madame Bovary 
- Mémoires d’un fou 
- Salammbô
- The Temptation of Saint Anthony 
- Three Tales

Source: Britannica.com

Ellis Bell was the pen name used by Emily Bronte. 

Emily Bronte:

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) Karl Marx was born in -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Karl Marx:
Karl Heinrich Marx was born in the Rhine province of Prussia, or in present-day Germany, in 1818.
- He was a revolutionary, sociologist, historian, and economist. He worked primarily in the realm of political philosophy and was a famous advocate for communism. 
-He is one of the most influential writers of communist movements books. 

Best Works; 
- Das Kapital 
- The Communist Manifesto. (Co-author with Friedrich Engels.)
These two books created the foundation of communist movement.

Ivanhoe: In full, Ivanhoe: A Romance .This is a historical novel by Sir Walter Scott.
Set in 12th-century England, with colourful descriptions of a tournament, outlaws, a witch trial, and divisions between Jews and Christians, Ivanhoe is credited for increased interest in chivalric romance and medievalism.

Main Characters:

- Lady Rowena
- Rebecca
- Cedric the Saxon

- Locksley
- Isaac of York
- Wilfred of Ivanhoe 

Sir Walter Scott: (1771-1832)
- He was Scottish but many of his works are based in England.
Job: He was appointed sheriff depute to the county of Selkirk in 1799 and was also a partner in a printing firm owned by the Ballantyne brothers.

Best Works:

Daily Quiz.option4: ঘ) The Picture of Dorian Gray
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Picture of Dorian Gray: The Picture of Dorian Gray is a philosophical/moral fantasy novel by Oscar Wilde.
A shorter novella-length version was published in the July 1890 issue of the American periodical Lippincott's Monthly Magazine.

Oscar Wilde (1856-1900) :
He was a poet,novelist and dramatist. This Irish born poet became London’s most popular playwright in the early 1890s. His full name was Oscar Fingal O’Flahertie Wills Wilde.
Oscar Wilde’s literary reputation rests largely on his novel.
- The Picture of Dorian Gray (1891) 
- Lady Windermere’s Fan (1892) 
- The Importance of Being Earnest (1895).

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) John Stuart Mill was born in-
Daily Quiz.exp:
John Stuart Mill:
- He was born on May 20, 1806 in London in England. 
- He was a renowned English Philosopher and political economist. He was the leading expositor of utilitarianism.

Utilitarianism: It is an ethical principle according to which an action is right if it tends to maximize happiness, not only that of the agent but also of everyone affected. 

Notable Works:

  • Essay on Economics and society (Article, 1967)
  • Utilitarianism (1863)
  • The Subjection of Women. (1869)
  • On Liberty (1859) 

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) History of England by Thomas Babington Macaulay is a combination of
Daily Quiz.exp:
History of England: (Written in 1849-61)

The History of England from the Accession of James the Second (1848) is the full title of the 05 Volume work by Lord Macaulay (1800–1859) more generally known as The History of England. 

It covers the 17-year period from 1685 to 1702, encompassing the reign of James II, the Glorious Revolution, the coregency of William III and Mary II, and up to William III's death.

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) Who of the following is a character from ‘Silas Marner’ by George Eliot?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Silas Marner:
In full, Silas Marner: The Weaver of Raveloe is the third novel by George Eliot. It was published in 1861. An outwardly simple tale of a linen weaver, the novel is notable for its strong realism and its sophisticated treatment of a variety of issues ranging from religion to industrialisation to community.

Major Characters:
- Silas Marner
- Squire Cass
- Dunstan Cass
- Eppie 
- Sarah
- Priscilla Lammete. Etc.

George Eliot(1819-80):
Her real name is Mary Ann Evans. She developed the psychological analysis of characters. 

Best Works: 
- Adam Bede (1859) 
- Silas Marner (1861) 
- Middlemarch (1871-72)
- Scenes of Clerical life (1858)
- The Mill on the Floss (1860)
- The Spanish Gypsy (tragi-comedy)

Source: Britannica.com
